# Starter Plan: Good Bread at Home

## The decision first: start with **both — but not the hard version of "both"**

BBC Good Food's own difficulty ratings make this call easy. In their [bread collection](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/collection/bread-recipes) (107 recipes), **Easy white bread** is rated *Easy* with 688 ratings. In the [sourdough collection](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/collection/sourdough-recipes), their **White sourdough** is rated *"A challenge"* — but **Easy sourdough bread** ("cheat's sourdough") is only *"More effort"*, because **it uses an overnight starter instead of a culture you feed for weeks.**

That's the loophole. You get a weekend sourdough loaf without adopting a pet.

- **Weekday loaf:** Easy white bread (yeasted)
- **Weekend loaf:** Cheat's sourdough — overnight starter, discarded after use
- **Defer to month 2+:** a real maintained starter and the "challenge" white sourdough

## The two recipes

**1. Easy white bread** — [bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/easy-white-bread](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/easy-white-bread)
500g strong white flour · 2 tsp salt · 7g fast-action yeast · 3 tbsp olive oil · 300ml water. Knead 10 min → rise 1 hr → shape → prove 1 hr → bake ~220°C/425°F for 25–30 min.

**2. Easy sourdough bread** — [bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/cheats-sourdough](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/cheats-sourdough)
Starter: mix ingredients with 250ml cold water, cover, **leave overnight (up to 24 hrs)**. Dough: add 1 tbsp fine salt + 200ml cold water, knead 10 min, rise 1 hr → shape round → prove 1 hr → bake 220°C with **ice cubes thrown into a tray underneath** for steam.

## Time commitment — the number that actually matters

**Easy white bread reads "2 hrs 50 mins," but only ~25 minutes is hands-on.** The rest is dough sitting in a bowl while you do something else. That single fact is what makes this non-intimidating.

Two scheduling tricks from the recipes themselves:
- **Fridge retard** (Step 4 of Easy white bread): after shaping, refrigerate overnight and bake in the morning. This is how bread fits a work week.
- The cheat's sourdough dough can rise **3 hrs in the fridge** instead of 1 hr at room temperature.

## The video: King Arthur Baking Company

Their **BREAD 101** series is a 3-parter from a genuinely reputable baking institution (386k subscribers):

- **[Part 1: kneading techniques](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5ZqJyalYqKU)** — 4:05, 327k views
- **[Part 3: shaping and baking the loaf](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yGb-hwg2OaU)** — 5:43, 684k views

**Ten minutes total.** Watch both before your first bake. Kneading and shaping are the two things text instructions genuinely fail to convey — everything else you can read.

## Is $180 realistic? Yes — and you should spend less

**You come in ~$55 under budget, and you can start for $60.** Both BBC recipes bake on an ordinary baking tray, so the Dutch oven is a genuine upgrade rather than a requirement. Buy Tier 1 now, add the Dutch oven when a freeform loaf frustrates you.

**Skip for now:**
- **Stand mixer** — 10 minutes of hand-kneading is the lesson, not the obstacle
- **Banneton and lame** — the cheat's sourdough recipe explicitly proves on floured parchment under a tea towel and slashes with *a utility knife*
- **A maintained starter** — the biggest quit-point in home baking, and the cheat's method sidesteps it entirely
- **Specialty flour, couche, proofing box, grain mill**

The single highest-value purchase is the **$13.99 scale**. Volume measuring is the most common cause of bad home bread, and 500g is 500g.

## First-week schedule

| Day | Task | Hands-on |
|---|---|---|
| **Sat Sep 5** | Order Tier 1 + 2. Watch both King Arthur videos. | 15 min |
| **Sun–Mon** | Delivery (estimates were Sep 6–10). | — |
| **Tue Sep 8, eve** | **Bake 1: Easy white bread**, in a loaf pan. Focus only on kneading to a smooth, springy dough. | ~25 min over 3 hrs |
| **Thu Sep 10** | **Bake 2: same recipe**, but shape at night and **retard in the fridge**; bake Friday morning. Proves the recipe fits a work week. | ~25 min, split |
| **Fri Sep 11, eve** | Mix the cheat's sourdough starter. Cover. Walk away. | 5 min |
| **Sat Sep 12** | **Bake 3: Easy sourdough**, freeform with the ice-cube steam trick. | ~30 min over 3 hrs |

Bake the *same* white loaf twice on purpose. The variable you're learning to read is proof — what "doubled in size" actually looks like — and you can only see that by repeating one recipe.

## Six techniques that carry everything

1. **Weigh, don't scoop.** Grams, always.
2. **Knead the full 10 minutes** (5–7 in a mixer). Stop when the dough is smooth, elastic and springy — Part 1 of the video shows the feel.
3. **Judge proof by size, not the clock.** "Doubled" beats "1 hour" in every kitchen.
4. **Shape with tension** (Part 3). This, not the recipe, determines whether a loaf rises or spreads.
5. **Steam for the first minutes.** Ice cubes in a preheated tray below — free crust.
6. **Bake to temperature.** Your thermometer removes the last guess; ~93–99°C / 200–210°F in the center.
